The notation used throughout the argument, collected for reference. Each symbol is defined in full where it is introduced; the italic tag at the end of an entry points to the section where it first appears.

## The Conditions

**T** · *Temporality *· The Condition of Reality such that succession is necessarily possible. *First use: [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4).*

**S** · *Spatiality *· The Condition of Reality such that distinction is necessarily possible. *First use: [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4).*

**Φ** · *Physicality *· The Condition of Reality such that exchange is necessarily possible. *First use: [§1.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4).*

**T(x), S(x), Φ(x)** · *Predicate form *· Applied to an individual *x*, each says that *x* instantiates the corresponding Condition.

**Exists(x)** · *Existence predicate *· Exists(x) =df T(x) ∧ S(x) ∧ Φ(x). To exist is to instantiate all three Conditions. *First use: [§1.5](groundwork.html#sec-1-5).*

## Structural terms

**C** · *Change *· Schematic letter for the change-event. *First use: [§1.3](groundwork.html#sec-1-3).*

**N** · *Nature *· N =df T ∧ S ∧ Φ. The definition is box-free; the necessity □(T ∧ S ∧ Φ) is the earned result Triconditional Necessity ([§2.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-5)). *First use: [§1.4.4](groundwork.html#sec-1-4-4).*

**R** · *Reality *· The totality of what is real, identified with Nature in □(R = N). *First use: [§1.1](groundwork.html#sec-1-1).*

**∅** · *Null State *· Absolute nothingness. *First use: [§2.7.1](the-argument.html#sec-2-7-1).*

**G** · *Classical God *· The Maximally Great Being, defined by negation of the structural roles: ¬T, ¬S, ¬Φ. Subject of the modal-ontological arguments ◇□G and ◇□¬G. *First use: [§6.1](relocating-greatness.html#sec-6-1).*

## Logical notation

**□** · *Necessity operator *· □P is true just when P holds across every configuration of Reality. *First use: [§1.2](groundwork.html#sec-1-2).*

**◇** · *Possibility operator *· ◇P is true just when P holds in at least one configuration of Reality. *First use: [§1.2](groundwork.html#sec-1-2).*

**∧ ∨ ¬ → ↔** · *Logical connectives *· Conjunction, disjunction, negation, material conditional, biconditional.

**∀ ∃** · *Quantifiers *· ∀ is the universal quantifier, read *for all*; ∃ is the existential quantifier, read *there exists*.

**∴** · *Therefore *· Reserved for the conclusion lines of formal syllogisms.

**=df** · *Defined as *· Introduces a stipulative definition.

## Variables

**P, Q** · *Propositional variables *· Schematic propositional variables, ranging over contentful claims. *First use: [§1.2](groundwork.html#sec-1-2).*

**w, w′, w₀, w₁, w₂, w∗** · *Possible-world variables *· w is the generic world; w′ the counterworld of the [§2.1.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-5) negation reductio; w₀ the candidate world posited to lack the structural Conditions at [§2.7.4](the-argument.html#sec-2-7-4); w₁, w₂, … enumerated worlds; w∗ the dual world introduced under bilateral symmetry at [§6.1](relocating-greatness.html#sec-6-1) and Appendix B item 16. *First use: [§2.1.5](the-argument.html#sec-2-1-5).*
